opening_message:
Ticket 1: Matthew Mejia (employee ID E034) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E034.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Matthew Mejia (E034) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires role ownership of the system, which does not apply here. Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security check: E034 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits the max to read. Requested write is above the max, so recommend read.
reason: Matthew Mejia (E034) requested write access to Payroll. The HR note lists them as full-time (max write), but the Security note, which looked up employment type and security training in its own database, lists them as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read only (write requires advanced training). Since the employment records conflict and the contractor status with basic training is the more restrictive verified fact, the maximum allowed level is read. Requested write exceeds this maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.
